Author: Sri Ramani Anna (in Tamil)
Source: Sakthi Vikatan issue dated Dec 20, 2006
Compiled by Jagadguru Sri Maha Periyava - Kanchi Paramacharya/Fb
It was early morning, many years ago. It was drizzling slightly. Sri Maha Periyava was seated in solitude at Kanchi Sri Sankara Matam. After the devotees had darshan of Him, Swami arose to go to His room. Just then an old grandmother and a young woman came running and prostrated to the sage. Swami sat down again, looking keenly at them.

With happiness on His face, Swami said, "Adede! Is it Meenakshi Patti? What a wonder you have come in the morning itself? Who is accompanying you? Is it your granddaughter? What is her name?"

Meenakshi Patti said “Periyava, I have been coming to Sri Matam for many years to have your darshan. Till now I have not got an opportunity to talk to you about myself. But such a need has come now. I have only one daughter. This girl is my granddaughter. Since she was born in this town and so we named her Kamakshi. My daughter passed away twelve years ago. Even before that my son-in-law died of heart attack. Hence I have been struggling to bring her up. I enrolled her in a school but she was was not good in studies. Hence she has left school after fifth class. Now she is fifteen years old. If I can get her married off, my responsibility will be over.”

Acharyal listened to her patiently and then asked, “You bring flowers everyday around 10 am for Chandramouliswara Pooja. Since you have come early this morning, I have understood that you come with a purpose. What is the matter?”

Hesitantly Meenakshi Patti said “Periyava, I have received a marriage proposal. The groom is a school teacher in this town. He earns a salary of Rs 60 per month. He is from a good family and the horoscopes are matching well. I pray to Periyava to arrange to conduct this marriage.”

Slightly annoyed Acharyal asked “What are you saying? You want me to conduct the marriage?” In a few seconds Periyava, calmed down and asked “Alright, What do you expect me to do?”

With relief Patti said “Periyavaa, I have managed to save five thousand rupees for her marriage and I can conduct the marriage within this amount. But groom’s mother is demanding that I should gift the bride a double-stringed, eight-sovereign gold chain. With my meagre income I have managed to buy only 2 gold bangles of one sovereign each for her. Only that is possible for me. Where can I go for an eight-sovereign double-stringed chain, Periyava? Only you…"

Before she could finish, Periyava asked with anger “Are you asking me to get a double-stringed chain in eight-sovereigns for your granddaughter?”

Meenakshi Patti prostrated to Periyava and rose. Patting her cheeks loudly, she said, "Apacharam, Apacharam, Periyava!. I am not asking Periyava to buy a gold chain. Many rich devotees come for your darshan every day. I only request you to ask one of those devotees to help me arrange for the eight-sovereign double-stringed chain?"

Periyava said “I don’t ask devotees for such financial help. I suggest that you look for an alliance within your means. That will be good for you.” Swamigal got up.

Meenakshi Patti said anxiously, "I pray that Periyava shouldn't leave me with such advice! This is a very good alliance, Periyava. The boy has a positive temperament. They got their own daughters married with a gift of an eight-sovereign double-stringed chain each. Therefore they desire that the girl coming as their daughter-in-law should also come with a double-stringed chain. Nothing else, Periyava. Only you should provide me with guidance in the matter!" Patti begged the sage.

Acharyal, who had got up, sat down again. He was immersed in deep thoughts for sometime. Then he started talking with compassion: "Will you do something I suggest now?"

"I will do it definitely. Please tell me what it is!" Patti was excited.

"Go to the Kamakshi Amman temple tomorrow with your granddaughter. Both of you pray to Her, 'This marriage should take place grandly with the required eight-sovereign double-stringed chain provided. Only You should arrange it, Amma!’ Do the “Pancha Sankya Upacharam” ie do pradakshina of the sannidhi five times, prostrate before Ambal five times and do this consecutively for five days. Goddess Kamakshi will arrange the things as you have desired in your mind." Acharyal blessed them with a smile.

As she prostrated and got up, Meenakshi Patti said, "What is it Periyava, you suggest everything five times!" She asked with eagerness, "If I do it that way, will Ambal Kamakshi surely arrange my granddaughter Kamakshi's marriage?"

"I am not suggesting the “Pancha Sankya Upacharam” myself. Ambal has the reverence of Pancha Sankhyopacharini. She grants favours happily when she is worshipped in multiples of five." Swamiji said, "I told you only that, nothing else!"

"When do we start this, Periyava?"

Swami smiled. "It has been said ‘shubhasya sheeghram’. Today is Friday. Why don’t you start today itself." He said and bade them farewell.

With her granddaughter beside her, Patti walked towards Kamakshi Amman temple. Since it was Friday, the temple was very crowded. Mother Kamakshi dazzled in full splendour with all the special adornments of that day. Both of them closed their eyes and prayed as advised by Periyava. Patti had an archana performed in her granddaughter's birth star and received the prasadam.

Then they both prayed to Amman about the eight-sovereign double-stringed chain and went around the inner courtyard clockwise five times. Then they prostrated to Ambal five times as Swamiji had suggested. With faith in their hearts, they went back home.

On Saturday morning, Patti started from her house with her granddaughter. Collecting the coral-jasmine flowers, she hurried to Sankara Matam. There was a heavy rush in the Matham. Meenakshi Patti was standing in the queue with some twenty or thirty devotees before her. She heard what the person before her was telling his neighbour with concern. “Today is the day of the Anusham star. Maha Periyava's birth star. So Swami has taken up a vow of silence today. He wouldn't talk to anybody. Only mukha darshan.”

Anxiety got hold of Meenakshi Patti. She was worried and thought 'I thought of reminding Periyava about the eight-sovereign double-stringed chain, but it seems that won't be possible now.' When they got near Periyava, they prostrated to Him. Periyava was sitting silently. Patti paused, yearning that He would ask something about the chain. Swami's assistant told her a bit sternly, "Patti, move away please! Periyava adopts a vow of silence today. He won't talk. See, how many people are waiting behind you!"

She made her way towards Kamakshi Amman temple, along with her granddaughter. As advised by Periyava, they performed the “Pancha Sankya Upacharam” worship on that day and got back home. Maha Swamiji continued the vow of silence on the following two days also. Patti and her granddaughter could only have a darshan of the sage at the Matham. Patti started worrying, 'Four out of five days has gone by since Periyava's advice but nothing happened! Will Mother Kamakshi open her eyes and bless me or not?' She could only grieve within herself.

It dawned on Tuesday. Sri Kanchi Matam was very brisk on that day. A bhajan troupe from Arani was immersing the Matham in bhaktic ecstasy.

Acharyal came and sat in his usual place. There was such a Maha Tejas on His face! He had dissolved his vow of silence. There was a large crowd waiting for Periyava's darshan. A middle-aged maami in the queue prostrated to Swami happily as her turn came. Happiness was writ all over her face. She submitted the things she had brought--a large bunch of rastali bananas, un-shorn coconuts, sweet lemons, oranges, pumpkins, and chubby raw-bananas--and prostrated again.

Swami smiled to himself as He glanced at the items kept before him. Then He narrowed His eyes and looked keenly at the woman. "Aren't you Ambujam, wife of Needamangalam landowner Ganesa Iyer? You came two months back. Told me something, feeling sad. Looking at the way you have come now with a large banana bunch, it seems that your problems would have been solved by the grace of Kamakshi, right?"

Ambujam prostrated again and said, "True, Periyava. My only daughter, Mythili was made to stay away from her husband's home for the last three years. Two months back I came running to you, reported this humiliation and wept. It was you who advised me to do “Pancha Sankya Upacharam” (five circumambulations and five prostrations for five days) and perform abhishekham (ablution) and worship in the Kamakshi Amman temple of this town. I completed them with extreme care, and what a wonder, fifteen days back, my son-in-law Radhakrishnan who works in Jamshedpur Tata Steel Plant came over himself and took his wife Mythili back with him. It's all that Kamakshi's grace and your blessings, Periyava!" Tears of joy filled her eyes as she spoke.

Swamiji said, "Besh, besh, very glad. Let the dampati rest in prosperity! By the way, where did you get such a big bunch of bananas? Looks massive!" Swamiji's laughed heartily.

Ambujam said smilingly, "This bunch was harvested from our own banana bed, Periyava; which is why it is so big!" She spoke with humility.

Showing happiness, Swami ordered her, "Alright, only Amma Kamakshi has united your daughter and son-in-law. So you offer this big banana bunch to Her and distribute the fruits to the devotees who visit the shrine."

Ambujam said, "No no, Periyava. Let it remain in this sanctum. I have another identical bunch to offer to Ambal. Now I seek your leave to have a darshan of Ambal, complete my prayers and get back here." She prostrated.

"Besha! After completing your prayers you must take food in the Matham and then only should get back to your place. Remember it!" Swamiji gave her His consent to leave Him.

There was not much crowd in Kamakshi Amman temple on that day. It was eleven in the morning. As it was later than usual, Meenakshi Patti hurried to the temple with her granddaughter. She halted at the shop selling archana packs, and told her granddaughter, "Hey Kamakshi! Today is the day of completion. So we shall do everything in five numbers as told by Acharyal. What you do, get five archana packs with five coconuts, five bananas, betel leaves, nuts, etc. and come back running!" and gave her the required money.

The granddaughter bought the things as ordered. Patti performed the archanas to Ambal and prayed Her with tearful eyes, 'Amma Kamakshi, I am completely depending on You only! I have no refuge except You and Swamigal. Only You should arrange for the eight-sovereign double-string chain and complete my granddaughter's marriage in a fitting manner.' As Patti sobbed, her granddaughter was also moved and wept. Then they started going round the inner couryard from left to right. They were on their fourth round.

"Patti... Patti... Patti!" Meekakshi Patti looked back at the loud call from her granddaughter and chided her angrily, "Why are you crying so loudly? What have you lost to raise such a noise?"

"Nothing lost Patti, but something gained! Please come here, I shall show you!" She took her grandmother to a corner, opened her right palm and showed her something. It was a severed, double-stringed chain with a front.

"Where did you find that?" Patti asked with surprise. Her granddaughter said, "As I was coming behind you with a bowed head, my eyes fell on this chain. I took it at once, and no one has noticed me! This chain is severed Patti. Check if it is genuine gold or just a gold-plated one."

Patti took the chain in her hands to estimate its weight. She said, "Looks like sovereign, Kamakshi! May be eight or eight-and-a-half sovereigns. This has been granted to us by Kamakshi Herself backed by the blessings of Periyava. Alright, let us go out first!" She packed the chain inside the edge of her sari and hurriedly came out, forgetting to complete her fifth circumambulation.

It was one in the afternoon. Four or five people were waiting for the darshan of Acharyal in the Matham. Meenakshi Patti prostrated to the sage with her granddaughter and got up. Swamiji looked at her and laughed. Paati was wondering if she should tell Periyavar about the chain that she found.

Swamiji foresaw her. "Today you should have completed your Pancha Sankyopachara pradakshina in order. But then, it was not completed because of some object that came to the hand of your granddaughter! That sudden delight did not allow you to do more than four pradakshinas. You came hurriedly, thinking that Kamakshi has given you Her full blessings. What, am I right?"

Patti was shocked. She became insensate, and swallowed her words as she spoke: "Swamigal shouldn't mistake me. Once that object came to the hand of my granddaughter, I assumed that Ambal Herself had dropped it for my granddaughter to take. In that sudden delight I totally fogot that I had to make one more pradakshina."

Periyava said relentlessly, "Did you forget only that? Did you not forget to get the chain weighed at Rangu Patthar's shop? Or get the severed portion melted in the furnace to rejoin it." He clinched His talk with the words, "Let it go. When you weighed it, was it exactly eight sovereigns?"

Patti and her granddaughter were stunned. "All you said now is the truth, Periyava!" said Patti.

Swamiji asked her calmly, "Tell me in fairness. To whom does that chain belong?"

"To Ambal Kamakshi."

"Tell me yourself, can you take it secretly and pack it inside the edge of your sari?"

"A mistake... nothing else but a mistake! Periyava should forgive me. I have done it out of ignorance." Patti was genuinely repenting. She placed the double-stringed sovereign chain on the brass plate that was found before Swamiji, her hands shaking. Swamiji laughed.

It was now two in the afternoon. Swamiji asked Meenakshi Patti and her daughter to sit before him. It was at that time that Ambujam Ammal, wife of Needamangalam Ganesa Iyer, who had taken leave in the morning, came back full of sorrow and prostrated to the sage. Her eyes were shedding tears profusely. Swamiji saw this and said affectionately, "Adada, why do you shed tears Amma?"

Ambujam Ammal wiped her tears and replied, "It is like this, Periyava. Two months ago when I did the five days seva in the Kamakshi Amman temple I prayed to Ambal earnestly that I would offer Her my eight-sovereign double-stringed chain if she united my daughter and son-in-law, who were then separated. Ambal has united them. I went to the temple to offer my chain. It slipped from my neck and fell down somewhere. I searched everywhere thoroughly but the chain could not be found. What can I do now, Periyava?" She started wailing.

Swami turned his face to Meenakshi Patti and looked meaningfully. Patti prostrated to Him and got up briskly. She took the double-stringed sovereign chain from the brass plate before the sage in her hand. She turned to Ambujam and said holding up the chain, "Amma Ambujam. Check if this is the double-stringed chain you lost."

Ambujam took the chain from her hand and checked. "The same, the same chain, Patti. How did it come here?" Patti narrated everything that happened to them in one breath.

Ambujam Ammal hugged Meenakshi Patti. "Patti, you don't worry at all! I am informing you this before our Acharyal. I shall arrange for a new double-stringed chain in eight sovereigns for your granddaughter! Her marriage will be performed grandly. This double-stringed I have prayed to offer to Ambal. This evening I shall take you and your granddaughter Kamakshi to the jewellery shop in this down and get her an eight-sovereign double-stringed chain. In addition, I shall give you five thousand rupees for the marriage expenses."

Swami was sitting as the Pratyaksha Kamakshi, witnessing this scene. Everyone prostrated to Acharyal. He looked at Meenakshi Patti and said, "Today you and your granddaughter have not done the five pradakshinas. Go in the evening, do five pradakshinas and five prostrations, and have a darshan of Ambal." Saying this he bid them farewell.

It is not possible to narrate in words the happiness and excitement felt by Meenakshi Patti and her granddaughter at that time.

AI Overview
These three names share a deep linguistic and historical connection, primarily originating in Ancient Mesopotamia, the Middle East, and the Caucasus.
Sargon
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Greek and biblical translation of the Akkadian regnal name Šarru-kīn. It combines šarru (Akkadian for "king") and kīnu (meaning "true," "established," or "legitimate").
Historical Significance: It is most famously associated with Sargon of Akkad (24th century BCE), the legendary founder of the Akkadian Empire. Later, the Neo-Assyrian ruler Sargon II (8th century BCE) adopted the throne name to establish the legitimacy of his rule.
Sargis
Origin & Etymology: The name is the Classical Syriac and Armenian form of the Latin name Sergius. It originates from the ancient Roman gens (clan) Sergia, which etymologists suspect may connect to the Latin verb servare ("to guard" or "to preserve").
Sako
Origin & Etymology: Sako operates on a few different historical tracks depending on the region:
In the Middle East: Among Assyrians and Armenians, Sako is a popular, affectionate diminutive (or pet form) of the proper name Sargis.
In the Balkans: In Albania, it functions as a standalone occupational surname for a "church servant" or as a nickname for the Muslim name Isak (Isaac).
In Asia: It is also an unrelated Japanese surname (written as 佐古) meaning "HELP" and "ancient".

INGLIS READY2RACE SALE: LOTS 51–100 REVIEW | STRONG PRICES, BUT CLEARANCE REMAINS A CONCERN

The second block of 50 lots generated $4.845 million in reported sales, with 24 horses sold, 15 passed in and 11 withdrawn. The average reached $201,875, while the median stood at $155,000. The clearance rate was 61.5% of lots offered and not withdrawn, highlighting the challenge of converting buyer interest into completed transactions.

💰 THE STANDOUT RESULTS

Lot 83, the Anamoe colt out of Really Discreet, topped this group at $600,000. Lot 97, the Written By colt out of Ruby Flo, realised $380,000. Lot 53, the Cosmic Force gelding out of Munjai, Lot 94, the Hellbent colt out of Romany Rocks, and Lot 100, the Alabama Express colt out of Rue Vivienne, each achieved $350,000.

Lot 81, the Captivant colt out of Rakitno, sold for $325,000, while Lot 63, the Sword of State colt out of Paris, made $320,000.

These seven transactions generated $2.645 million, approximately 55% of the total gross. Once again, a relatively small number of high-value sales accounted for a substantial proportion of turnover.

📊 THE DATA TELLS THE STORY

The $201,875 average exceeded the $155,000 median, reflecting the influence of expensive individuals on the overall figures. However, the 61.5% clearance rate demonstrates that demand remains selective, with 15 horses failing to meet their reserves.

The contrast between Lot 83 at $600,000 and several horses selling for $50,000 or less illustrates the wide variation in buyer valuations across the catalogue.

THE VERDICT: Lots 51–100 produced a higher average and median than the opening 50 lots, but the clearance rate fell from 68.3% to 61.5%. The top end remains capable of generating significant money, yet the results underline the importance of realistic reserves and disciplined purchasing.

For vendors preparing two-year-olds, headline prices mean little without accounting for acquisition and preparation costs. For buyers, the challenge is identifying genuine value rather than simply paying a premium for pedigree or breeze-up performance.

The money is being spent, but the market is not accepting every price. The real test for the 2026 Inglis Ready2Race Sale is whether competitive bidding can translate into stronger clearance across the remaining catalogue.

Below is a list of some national, international, global and local observances for October 15, 2026:

International Day of Rural Women (UN observance since the 2007 General Assembly resolution) honors the contributions of rural women to agriculture, food security, and biodiversity, noting they comprise nearly 40% of the global agricultural workforce yet own far less land and receive lower pay. If women had equal access to productive resources, farm yields could rise 20–30%, potentially feeding an additional 100–150 million people—an economic argument that frames gender equity as a practical food-security tool.⁠
UN

National Grouch Day celebrates the permission to embrace irritability, complaining, and general grumpiness without judgment, often linked to Oscar the Grouch, though its true origin was a 1976 practical joke by a Michigan sixth-grader and her grandparents at Chase’s Calendar of Events, who named it for her notoriously grouchy teacher’s birthday on October 15 and even made him honorary president of a fictional National Association of Grouches. Intriguingly, Oscar himself debuted orange in the first season of Sesame Street and only turned green after a fictional vacation in a swamp that left him “moldy,” while his trash can is canonically larger inside, containing a swimming pool, ice rink, and bowling alley.⁠ Daysoftheyear

National I Love Lucy Day marks the October 15, 1951, CBS premiere of the sitcom starring Lucille Ball and Desi Arnaz as Lucy and Ricky Ricardo, which became the first scripted show filmed on 35mm with multiple cameras before a live audience, pioneering techniques still used today and proving the value of syndication after Ball and Arnaz retained ownership of the negatives. A thought-provoking detail is that CBS executives initially resisted casting Arnaz due to his Cuban accent and background, prompting the couple to take a successful live vaudeville tour to prove audiences would accept them; the January 19, 1953, episode in which Lucy gives birth drew about 44 million viewers (roughly 72% of TV households) and even outdrew President Eisenhower’s inauguration coverage the day before, coinciding with Ball’s real-life delivery of Desi Arnaz Jr.⁠ History

Spirit Day (observed on the third Thursday of October) is an international awareness day promoting support for LGBTQ+ youth against bullying, founded in 2010 by Canadian high-school student Brittany McMillan after she saw a wave of news about youth suicides, including Tyler Clementi’s, and posted on Tumblr urging people to wear purple (the color Gilbert Baker assigned to “spirit” on the rainbow flag). What began as a local student call quickly went viral, drawing GLAAD’s partnership and millions of participants; early years saw celebrities and even websites turning purple, and one Arkansas school-board official’s anti-gay Facebook posts in response led to his resignation after national backlash.⁠ Wikipedia

Conflict Resolution Day (third Thursday in October) encourages peaceful approaches to disagreements and was established in 2005 by the Association for Conflict Resolution to highlight mediation, dialogue, and nonviolent problem-solving skills in schools, workplaces, and communities. A deeper angle is that it coincides with broader October observances around bullying prevention and equity, framing conflict not merely as something to avoid but as an opportunity for skill-building that can reduce the very isolation and hostility Spirit Day also addresses.

Global Handwashing Day promotes washing hands with soap as a simple, high-impact public-health practice that can cut diarrheal disease incidence by roughly 30% and acute respiratory infections by up to 20%, potentially preventing hundreds of thousands of child deaths annually; every dollar invested can return 35–92 times its value through reduced healthcare costs and productivity gains. The day was launched in 2008 by the Global Handwashing Partnership, and research shows handwashing education alone can reduce school absenteeism from gastrointestinal illness by 29–57%.⁠ CDC

World Students’ Day honors the birth anniversary of Indian aerospace scientist and former president A.P.J. Abdul Kalam (born October 15, 1931), celebrated especially in India with educational events, science outreach, and tributes to his role inspiring youth in science and teaching. The choice of date links a national scientific icon to a global call for valuing students, underscoring how individual curiosity scaled into national technological progress.

National Lemon Bar Day celebrates the classic American dessert of buttery shortbread crust topped with tangy lemon curd, founded in 2019 by Michael McCarthy after he brought them to a bake sale and discovered many people had never tasted one. The first widely circulated recipe appeared in the Chicago Daily Tribune on August 27, 1962 (submitted by Eleanor Mickelson), followed by a near-identical version in Betty Crocker’s 1963 Cooky Book that helped popularize the treat nationwide.⁠Checkiday

Get to Know Your Customers Day (third Thursday of each quarter) urges businesses to engage more personally with patrons beyond transactions, created around 2011 by Lynn B. Johnson during Customer Appreciation Month. The floating date ensures it lands on a weekday when interactions are possible, turning an abstract business principle into a concrete calendar reminder that relationships, not just sales, sustain enterprises.

National Pregnancy and Infant Loss Remembrance Day provides space to honor babies lost to miscarriage, stillbirth, SIDS, or other causes, founded in the early 2000s by Robyn Bear, Lisa Brown, and Tammy Novak after Bear’s multiple miscarriages left her without community support; Congress passed a supporting resolution in 2006, building on President Reagan’s 1988 designation of October as awareness month. Participants worldwide light candles at 7 p.m. local time for an “International Wave of Light,” creating a continuous global vigil that makes private grief briefly visible and shared.⁠ Wikipedia

National Cheese Curd Day honors the fresh, squeaky young cheddar pieces beloved in Wisconsin and the Midwest, launched in 2015 by the Culver’s restaurant chain. The signature squeak occurs only when the curds are fresh (ideally within a day and at room temperature) because elastic protein strands still bound by calcium rub against tooth enamel; once refrigerated longer, the squeak fades even if the flavor remains, making the sound itself a freshness test that locals use to judge quality.⁠ Prnewswire

National Mushroom Day celebrates edible fungi for their culinary umami, nutrition, and ecological roles (mycorrhizal networks, decomposition). Fungi are genetically closer to animals than to plants and, like humans, take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide; white button, cremini, and portobello mushrooms are actually the same species harvested at different stages, and some species (such as “chicken of the woods”) are prized for tasting remarkably like poultry.⁠Ibtimes

National Aesthetician (or Esthetician) Day recognizes skincare professionals who perform facials, peels, and related treatments, founded in 2016 by the brand COSMEDIX. The dual spelling reflects regional and professional preferences, and the day sits inside Breast Cancer Awareness Month, linking everyday skin health to broader wellness conversations.

White Cane Safety Day (also called Blind Americans Equality Day) commemorates the independence symbolized by the white cane for people who are blind or have low vision; Congress authorized the annual presidential proclamation in 1964, and President Lyndon B. Johnson issued the first one within hours of the joint resolution’s passage. The white color was chosen for visibility, and the day has evolved from primarily traffic-safety messaging toward broader recognition of mobility, equality, and self-reliance.⁠ Wikipedia

International Credit Union Day (third Thursday in October) celebrates member-owned cooperative financial institutions and has been observed since 1948. Its floating placement ensures it falls mid-week when branches and community events can occur, underscoring the cooperative model’s emphasis on local ownership and lower-cost services compared with traditional banks.

National Get Smart About Credit Day (third Thursday in October) educates young people on responsible credit use, launched in 2003 by the American Bankers Association Foundation with volunteer bankers providing counseling. The date aligns with other October financial-literacy and student-focused observances, treating credit knowledge as a preventable life skill rather than an adult afterthought.

National Shawarma Day celebrates the Middle Eastern vertical-rotisserie meat dish (name derived from an Arabic root meaning “to turn”), founded in 2020 by the Canadian chain Osmow’s, whose Egyptian-immigrant founder converted a sub shop after a customer requested a taste of the family lunch he was preparing. For the inaugural year the chain offered throwback $5 pricing echoing its 2001 opening, inviting other restaurants to join and framing the day as cultural exchange through street food.⁠ Strategyonline

National Pug Day salutes the ancient Chinese companion breed (origins at least to the Song dynasty, possibly earlier), created in 2012 by pet-lifestyle expert Colleen Paige to encourage adoption from rescues rather than breeders, given the breed’s health vulnerabilities as a brachycephalic dog. A historical highlight is the 1572 story of a pug named Pompey that allegedly alerted William of Orange to assassins, after which pugs gained favor with European royalty including Queen Victoria. ⁠Anydayguide

International ShakeOut Day (third Thursday in October) organizes the world’s largest coordinated earthquake drill, practicing “Drop, Cover, and Hold On” for at least one minute (often at 10:15 a.m. local time); it grew from the 2008 Great California ShakeOut and now involves tens of millions of participants globally. The fixed weekday maximizes school and workplace participation while allowing individuals to register drills on other dates if needed.⁠ Shakeout

National Latino (or Latinx) AIDS Awareness Day raises awareness of HIV prevention, testing, and treatment in Hispanic and Latinx communities in the United States and territories, founded in 2003 by the Latino Commission on AIDS and Hispanic Federation and timed to the close of Hispanic Heritage Month. The observance addresses documented disparities in infection rates and access while promoting open dialogue and testing.

National Chicken Cacciatore Day honors the Italian “hunter-style” braised chicken dish (cacciatore meaning “hunter”), typically prepared with tomatoes, onions, peppers, and herbs. The name evokes the rustic, foraged ingredients historically used by hunters, turning a simple weeknight meal into a calendar-worthy celebration of peasant cooking that traveled with Italian immigrants.

My Mom Is a Student Day recognizes mothers balancing parenting with formal education. The observance is relatively obscure, yet it highlights a demographic whose dual roles challenge assumptions about student life and family structure.

Breast Health Day falls within Breast Cancer Awareness Month and focuses on screening, self-awareness, and overall breast wellness. Its placement on the 15th keeps attention on preventive health amid the denser cluster of food and pop-culture days.

National Real Sugar Day: A recently established observance that also lands on October 15 to celebrate the history and harvest of real sugar.

Additional floating or less-centralized observances landing on this third Thursday include National HSA Awareness Day (Health Savings Accounts), and various local or niche celebrations such as National Roast Pheasant Day (tied to the start of the shooting season) and Sewing Lovers Day. Hispanic Heritage Month also concludes on October 15.

DETAILED SUMMARY
VATICAN OFFICIALS TRIED LEAKING THE THIRD SECRET OF FATIMA AND NO ONE LISTENED
From Anthony Stine, 13 October 2026, @ReturnToTradition (YouTube)

Today (Oct 13) is the 109th anniversary of the Miracle of the Sun, which occurred on October 13, 1917. The three Fatima children, together with tens of thousands of local witnesses and some from a distance, observed the sun appear to dance across the sky along with other extraordinary details. Stine focuses on the Third Secret of Fatima and does not accept that the version released around 2000 was complete or fully accurate. Multiple bishops, cardinals, and their expert advisers who were present when the secret was read stated that it concerned an apostasy in the Church led from the top. The published text instead presented a vision more readily associated with war-related apocalyptic events. That vision may have been metaphorical, with its explanatory text never released, or the released material may represent only a partial account. Stine has previously addressed the Fatima message and Miracle of the Sun in other episodes.

CLERGY ON THE THIRD SECRET (2:52–5:58)

The Fatima Center has highlighted a statement made on September 10, 1984, by Bishop of Fatima Alberto Cosme Amaral during a question-and-answer session at the Technical University of Vienna. The bishop said the secret of Fatima speaks neither of atomic weapons nor nuclear warheads, nor of Pershing missiles nor SS-20s. Its content concerns only the faith. To identify the secret with catastrophic announcements or with nuclear war is to deform the meaning of the message. The loss of faith of a continent is worse than the annihilation of a nation, because a continent can recover while souls lost to perdition remain lost forever. Faith continues to diminish in Europe.

A recent, lengthy LifeSite News article by Marian Soul, titled “The Final Confrontation: Examining the End Times Through the Lens of Fatima and Benedict XVI,” is examined. Toward its end the article surveys bishops and cardinals who sought to release or hint at the content of the Third Secret. Father Charles Murr has recently appeared on podcasts arguing that Benedict XVI was coerced into resigning and that, under a plain reading of the Code of Canon Law, such a resignation is invalid. Stine notes that Murr has not presented a concrete “smoking gun,” yet the position is part of the broader discussion.

APOSTASY AND THE PAPACY (5:58–13:21)

The LifeSite article records consistent testimony. Cardinal Oddi, a personal friend of Pope John XXIII who had discussed the secret with him, told an Italian journalist in 1990 that the Third Secret has nothing to do with Gorbachev; the Blessed Virgin was alerting the Church against apostasy within it. Cardinal Ciappi, personal papal theologian to John XXIII, Paul VI, John Paul I, and John Paul II, stated that the great apostasy in the Church will begin at the top. Bishop Amaral of Fatima gave a similar indication. 

Father Gabriel Amorth, former chief exorcist of Rome who knew Padre Pio for 26 years, attributed to Padre Pio a sorrowful remark around 1960 that Satan has been introduced into the bosom of the Church and will within a short time come to rule a false church, a kind of Antichrist. This would explain John XXIII’s reluctance to publish the secret, lest people conclude he was an antipope. Padre Pio was tormented far more by the great apostasy within the Church than by other prophesied calamities.

These figures, spanning the ideological spectrum and including some present at the reading of the secret, testified to the same substance. An apostasy led from the top implies the emergence of a false church—the “ape of the Church” described by Fulton Sheen and by mystics such as Blessed Anne Catherine Emmerich and Marie Julie Jahenny. 

A counterfeit edifice is built over the true Church while the latter is dismantled from within; most people accept the false structure as the Catholic Church until only a tiny remnant remains, at which point God intervenes. Many accept the erroneous idea that the Holy Spirit personally chooses each pope. That view would require believing the Holy Spirit explicitly chose historically evil men who used the papacy for grave personal sins, including turning the Vatican into a bordello, while generally leaving the deposit of faith untouched. 

Benedict XVI stated that the Holy Spirit does not choose the pope; the cardinals may prayerfully seek His influence, yet free will and politicking at conclaves determine the outcome. Such dynamics make possible a pope or successive popes who lead an apostasy from the top.

THEOLOGY OF TYCONIUS (13:21–19:42)

Benedict XVI indicated that the theology of Tyconius can help the Church understand how to expose and defeat false brethren hidden within her. Tyconius’s insights overlap with the Fatima message. In 1956 Joseph Ratzinger published an essay on Tyconius’s concept of the Church. Tyconius, a fourth-century Donatist from North Africa, saw the Church as a bipartite body: one part belonging to Christ and another to the devil. The Antichrist belongs to the Church, grows in it and with it until the great discessio that initiates the final revelation. Ratzinger observed that the Church cannot survive if it passively defers the resolution of the conflict between its two bodies to the end of time. The internal battle has been underway for decades, with roots in nineteenth-century liberalism that applied revolutionary political values to theology and created a de facto schism.

In his general audience of April 22, 2009, Benedict designated Tyconius a great theologian and noted that Tyconius saw the Apocalypse as a reflection of the mystery of the Church. Tyconius held that the Church belongs to Christ yet contains another part that belongs to the devil. 

Stine asks to whom figures such as Cardinal McCarrick, Annibale Bugnini, Cardinal Bernardin, or contemporary leaders who urge the Church to adopt worldly values on family and gender actually belong. Benedict’s eschatological outlook draws heavily on Tyconius and supplies a missing link for understanding both the present crisis and his own resignation. The Marian Soul writer places the word “resignation” in quotation marks and appears to hold a Benevacantist position. Ratzinger had already explored Tyconius’s paradox of a man who places himself outside concrete ecclesiastical communion while still believing he belongs to the true Church. 

Benedict’s 2009 remarks effectively invited listeners to examine Tyconius’s Exposition of the Apocalypse, written around AD 390, the first substantial commentary on the final book of Scripture and one that shaped Latin interpretation for roughly eight hundred years.

THE BIPARTITE CHURCH (19:42–25:58)

Tyconius postulated two cities in the world, one of God and one of the devil. Humanity is not neatly segregated; the people of the devil are also divided, so that the Church is called a third part, the false brothers another third, and the heathen world a third. Babylon, the city of the devil, exists both among the heathen and among false brothers—those who outwardly profess Catholicism or Christianity yet are ravening wolves. They wrap evils in the language of the Gospel, promoting, for example, progressive political positions on the environment, immigration, or capital punishment, and thereby generate a new false religion. The city of the devil therefore exists both outside and inside the Church. 

This bipartite structure has always been present: the sons of Judas, monster popes who scandalized the faithful through personal vice yet rarely attempted to alter the deposit of faith itself (as in the tenth-century period of extreme impurity and simony). 

David Robinson, in the introduction to the English translation of Tyconius’s Exposition, notes that the Church is both black and beautiful, good and evil, enemy and beloved. In one body there are two parts, one persevering and the other transgressing. The good are mixed with the evil until the end of time; the Church will not spew out every evil person, but only some, so as to show the world what the last persecution will be like. There are two buildings in the Church, one built upon rock and another upon sand. False brothers confess Christ with their mouths but by their actions declare that they have no king except Caesar. Blasphemy exists not only among the kings of the world but inside the Church itself. 

The same pattern runs from Cain and Abel through the sons of Noah, Ishmael and Isaac, Esau and Jacob, the kingdoms of Judah and Israel, Judas among the Twelve, the weeds and the wheat, the net of good and bad fish, the wise and foolish virgins, and the sheep and the goats. In the Apocalypse the angelic messages to the seven churches repeatedly identify an unholy element within. The central theme of Tyconius’s commentary is the Church’s continual clash with the devil, especially the war waged inside the Church.

THE GREAT FALLING AWAY (25:58–34:34) 

Tyconius’s primary concern is the historical and spiritual conflict between the Lord’s body and the devil’s body, which he frequently calls the enemy body or anti-church. The anti-church masquerades as the Church, echoing Blessed Anne Catherine Emmerich’s vision of a false edifice erected over the true Church while the latter is dismantled from behind the scenes. Both the bride of Christ and the bride of Babylon are adorned with gold, silver, and precious stones, so that the devil’s body imitates the Lord’s body and deceives by similarity of splendor. Tyconius identifies this enemy body with the mystery of iniquity and the abomination of desolation. It will be fully revealed only at the time of the great discessio—the Latin term used by St. Jerome in translating 2 Thessalonians 2:3: “unless the discessio comes first and the man of sin be revealed.” 

Many English versions render the word as apostasy or revolt; it carries the sense of a falling away or separation. Only at that moment will the bipartite condition of the world be fully displayed in a tripartite division: the true Church, the false Church, and the heathen world. Before the falling away, everyone is considered the people of God; afterward the third part of the people of God appears. Only then is the distinction between true and false Church made manifest, and only then are God’s true people revealed. 

Commenting on Apocalypse 8:12 (a third part of the sun, moon, and stars stricken so that a third part of the day appears as night), Tyconius explains that the sun, moon, and stars represent the Church; “third” is a designation rather than a strict quantity. There are two parts in the Church, one of the day and one of the night. The Church was stricken—handed over to its own desires—so that as sins become more abundant and extreme the distinction would be revealed in due time. False brethren appear to belong to the city of God yet actually belong to the devil and inhabit Babylon spiritually; they remain outwardly unrecognizable until the Church is stricken by the discessio. 

Most arrestingly, Tyconius asserts that the great falling away of the end times will invert the conventional understanding of the term. Faithful Christians ordinarily assume that apostasy means droves of unbelievers leaving the Church. 

Tyconius holds the opposite: the true believers withdraw from the unfaithful within the Church. The bride of Christ, the mystical body, pulls away from those who are unfaithful. The true Church herself effects the great apostasy as a means of salvation from her enemies, forcing the already apostate body of the devil into the light. 

Expounding Apocalypse 16:19 (“the great city was divided into three parts”), Tyconius states that the great city is all people under heaven, who will be divided into the heathen, the abomination of desolation, and the Church which will have gone out from the midst of her. On the heavenly voice commanding “Go out from her, my people,” he notes that Babylon consists of external and internal parts, out of which the holy people will leave once clearly warned by God. In practice this may already be occurring when Catholics refuse to treat certain bishops as true officers of the Church.

THE PASSION OF THE CHURCH (34:34–44:24)  

Antonio Socci, an Italian journalist of repute, wrote The Fourth Secret of Fatima. He began the book intending to debunk the claim that the Third Secret had never been fully released and concluded that the claim was correct. He has also written on the resignation of Benedict XVI. 

Socci analyzes Tyconius’s theology: the Latin word discessio means a separation, division, cleavage, or withdrawal. The cleavage results from a withdrawal in which the mystical body of Christ extracts herself from the mystery of iniquity in order to expose the evil veiled within her and subsequently defeat it in the final persecution. The mystery of lawlessness, long held back and hidden inside the Church, comes out and reaches its zenith in the figure of the Antichrist. 

Tyconius maintains that the body of Christ will, for all practical purposes, activate and initiate her own passion. Before the falling away, everyone is considered the people of God; afterward the third part appears. The saints endure and faithfully preach; the false brothers are unmasked when they turn and persecute the Church. Those in league with the devil, although claiming to be Christians, fight against the Church. Persecution finally and completely reveals the identity of the saints and the false brothers. 

A natural question is whether, at the time of the predestined apostasy, the faithful will immediately recognize the false brethren and break off affiliation, or whether genuine believers will be persuaded to remain in association with the impostors. 

Tyconius is emphatic that these false brethren are often found among the Church’s leaders, the bishops. Commenting on Apocalypse 13:11 (another beast coming up out of the land with two horns similar to a lamb yet speaking as a snake), he describes a lamb that carries on after a snake has secretly inserted its venom. The figure fashions himself into a lamb through which disguise he attacks a secure lamb; he speaks for God through which disguise he turns seekers of God away from the way of truth. The Lord warned of false prophets who come in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves. The bishops do under the guise of a gift of the Church what advances the will of the devil. They offer the beast the veneer of a lamb while he uses them as a mouthpiece for his agenda. On the three unclean spirits proceeding from the mouth of the dragon, the beast, and the false prophet, Tyconius remarks that the dragon (the devil), the beast (the body of the devil), and the false prophets (the bishops of the body of the devil) are one spirit. The throne of the beast is his church on account of the duplicitous bishops under his sway—the ape church after the discessio. Those treacherous bishops give shape and form to the devil’s body even after the true Church has detached herself from it.

During his May 2010 pilgrimage to Fatima, Benedict XVI was asked what meaning the Fatima apparitions have for today and whether the vision of the suffering pope could be extended beyond the attack on John Paul II to other sufferings of the Church. His reply was striking: beyond the great vision of the suffering of the pope (which can in the first place refer to John Paul II), an indication is given of realities involving the future of the Church that are gradually taking shape and becoming evident. 

There is seen the need for a passion of the Church, which is reflected in the person of the pope. The sufferings of the Church are announced; the Lord told us the Church would constantly be suffering in different ways until the end of the world. Attacks on the pope and the Church come not only from without; the sufferings of the Church come precisely from within the Church, from the sin existing within the Church. 

The greatest persecution of the Church arises from sin within the Church. This is something always known but today seen in a really terrifying way. By stating that the vision can refer to John Paul II “in the first place,” Benedict implies that it is not limited to him alone. Stine notes that “attacks on the pope” here do not mean ordinary criticism but attempts to control the papacy or coerce a resignation, as illustrated in the plot of Malachi Martin’s novel Windswept House, in which antagonists seek to force John Paul II’s resignation so that a man of their own making can become pope. Stine recommends the book and asks where the present moment stands in that timeline.

CRITIQUE OF CHURCH HIERARCHY (44:24–51:38) 

The hierarchy constantly addresses political issues. The only sins now regularly named are sins against migrants and sins against the environment; theology is framed in progressive secular politics. A current example is Detroit Archbishop Edward Weisenberger. 

During a Synodal listening session on the environment at Sacred Heart Major Seminary in Detroit on September 30, he stated that sins against creation are among the very serious sins that cry out to heaven for justice. He criticized the Trump administration for cutting tax incentives for U.S.-made electric vehicles, implying that gas-powered cars damage creation, and said Catholics must follow Pope Leo and Pope Francis in emphasizing the environment and creation. 

Participants were invited to implement practices grounded in Pope Francis’s 2015 encyclical Laudato Si’. Stine notes that Laudato Si’ does not merely restate the scriptural principle of stewardship or the duty not to trash creation—points no Christian denies. It argues extensively for a new order of the ages, a world order administered by the United Nations with enforcement mechanisms for international agreements that compel non-cooperating countries (de facto the United States) to comply. Input from the session will be compiled and forwarded through the National Catholic Temperature Covenant to the Vatican. 

Stine regards this as radical environmentalism and a new religion—the ape of the Church. Treating failure to subsidize electric vehicles as a very serious sin, especially amid a contentious Michigan Senate race, illustrates the point. Many of the encyclical’s alarmist claims about temperature and effects on the poor have been challenged. Souls are at stake if such teaching is accepted as authentically Catholic.

SSPX APPEAL UPDATE (51:38–53:59) 

On the day of the broadcast the Priestly Society of St. Pius X issued a communiqué from its general house concerning the appeal against the decree of excommunication issued on July 2. Published on the English-language news site https://t.co/xm5ZX9QO5i, the statement notes that, further to the July 13 announcement of a preliminary request to the Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith, the Society has pursued the avenues of recourse provided by canon law in accordance with the established deadlines and procedures. 

Through these steps the bishops of the Society seek to exercise the right recognized to them by the Church, requesting an examination of the juridical and doctrinal objections they have raised against the text of July 2. Pending further action by the competent authorities, the Society intends to observe the discretion required by the nature of the proceedings. It invites priests and faithful to remain united in prayer for the Holy Father and the whole Church. The supreme law is the salvation of souls. 

The communiqué is dated Menzingen, October 13, 2026. Its practical effect is to remind both the faithful and Roman authorities that an appeal has been duly submitted and that, under the law, the Society has a right to have that appeal heard. Stine does not expect a response from the relevant dicastery head, which in theory should automatically advance the matter to the next stage before the Apostolic Signatura. Many officials across the ideological spectrum share a general hostility toward the SSPX.

5 independent colleges join as founding members of new US accreditor

By Jon Brown, Christian Post Reporter Tuesday, October 13, 2026

Benedictine College, a private liberal arts college in Atchison, Kansas, is one of the five independent colleges that joined as founding members of the National Association for Academic Excellence (NAAE). | Courtesy NAAE
Five independent colleges announced Tuesday that they have joined as founding members of the National Association for Academic Excellence (NAAE), a new U.S. institutional accreditor for colleges and universities that aims to provide an affirming place for faith-based institutions.

“Higher education accreditation is responsible to the Department of Education for the quality of institutions, and as a new accreditor, we hope to dramatically improve the quality of accreditation and the quality of higher education as a result,” Rob Manzer, president and CEO of NAAE, told The Christian Post.

Founded in 2023 as a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, NAAE Inc. began in response to shifts in higher education policy, including the U.S. Department of Education eliminating the distinction between regional and national accreditors by removing geographic scope from the federal recognition criteria in 2020.

Among the schools joining NAAE are Merrimack College, an Augustinian school in North Andover, Massachusetts; Benedictine College in Atchison, Kansas; the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York City; Bellevue University in Bellevue, Nebraska; and Houston Christian University in Texas.

Manzer, who was appointed as NAAE’s first president and CEO in March, told CP that throughout his more than 30-year career in higher education, the accreditation process invariably seemed like “box-checking compliance,” instead of something that leads to institutional improvement. NAAE’s accreditation offers something “structurally different,” he said.

“We are not building a region-based accreditor or a territory-based accreditor. That’s probably more important than anything else, I would say,” he said. “We are building something that is not based on a region, but that is consequentially collective. We are only going to work with independent colleges that meet our standards.”

The founding members will hold seats on NAAE’s Board of Directors and its Commission on Accreditation, which will make decisions about accreditation and help refine standards, procedures, training, technology, evidence requirements and terminology.

Manzer explained that NAAE's four standards, which are designed for independent colleges, cover ethics and integrity; organizational efficiency; academic excellence, including curriculum, faculty, learning outcomes and intellectual diversity; and service to students. He noted the foundation of their standards is the ideal that education ought to help students become better human beings.

“There are four standards, that’s it,” he said. “So schools are, through a process of self-reflection, having to show that they meet those standards. Now, here’s the most important point: for us, academic excellence is in service of the formation of the whole human person.”

text:
The afternoon light had already begun its long westward lean when I turned the car onto the narrow road that led out of town. A slight breeze moved through the open window, dry and clean in the way West Texas air often is after the heat of the day has started to loosen its grip. It carried the scent of honeysuckle from somewhere along the fence lines and the sharper resin of pine trees that stood in scattered clusters beyond the fields. Underneath those two notes ran something softer, a faint sweetness that caught me before I could name it—lilac, or the ghost of it, the same quiet floral edge of the body spray she used to wear. The fragrance seemed to gather in the cab of the truck and then spill out again with every breath of wind, so that by the time I reached the cemetery the air itself felt full of her. It was as if she had stepped into the space just ahead of me and left the ordinary landscape marked with her presence. For a moment the dry grass, the low stones, the open sky all seemed less empty than they should have been.

I parked and walked the uneven path with the guitar case bumping lightly against my leg, the cane steadying each step. The same breeze continued across the rise, lifting strands of hair across my forehead and stirring the faded petals of the artificial flowers someone had left beside her marker. When I lowered myself onto the grass the ground gave a little beneath me, cool through the fabric of my jeans. The lilac note lingered, faint but unmistakable, and the feeling that she was all around me settled deeper—not as a sudden apparition, but as a quiet, persistent nearness, the way a familiar scent can make an empty room feel occupied. I opened the case, settled the guitar across my lap, and let my fingers find the shapes they already knew. The first notes of “Always on My Mind” rose thin against the wind, and the breeze seemed to carry them outward the same way it had carried her scent inward.

I sang it the way I had sung it in the kitchen that first night, half-lit, the sink still dripping behind her. She had turned from the dishes with her hands still wet, and by the second verse her eyes had filled. She did not wipe them. She simply stood there listening, the water drying on her wrists, and afterward she laughed once—short, surprised—and told me I had no right to sound like that if I meant to do it only once. I did it again. Some evenings she asked; some evenings I offered before she could. The song became the small, quiet bridge we crossed when the rest of the day had been too sharp or too ordinary. Now the wind lifted strands of hair across my face and carried the last chord out over the low rise. I stayed where I was after the strings went quiet. The air still held that faint lilac sweetness beneath the honeysuckle and pine, and the feeling of her nearness did not leave.

I thought of the nights we simply sat up together. The apartment would be dim, the street outside reduced to the occasional sweep of headlights across the ceiling. One of us on the couch, the other in the chair that faced the window. Sometimes the television muttered on low; sometimes we left it dark. Those hours held almost no conversation and almost no decision. They held only the soft sound of her shifting, the faint creak of the floorboards when she rose to refill a glass, the ordinary and astonishing fact of two people remaining in the same room while the evening finished itself. I remembered the warmth of her shoulder against mine when she leaned, the way her breathing would slow and deepen until it matched the quiet of the room. Those stretches felt, in memory, like the truest measure of what we had managed to keep.

There were the other nights as well, the ones that required repair. Words would leave my mouth already sharpened—“Leave. Don’t come back.”—and she would stand in the doorway with her bag half-zipped, the strap biting into her shoulder. The air between us would thicken. I could hear my own pulse and still not know, in that exact moment, whether I meant the sentence or only the temporary relief of saying it. She always left for a while. She always came back. And I always found, later, the chance to apologize. The pattern had felt sturdy enough that I stopped counting how often we used it. Sitting there with the guitar still warm across my knees, the breeze still moving, I understood how small and fragile that pattern had been all along, how much of our time together had rested on the simple, repeated mercy of another morning.

And then there were the nights that required nothing at all. We would start a movie neither of us particularly wanted to finish and end up closer on the couch than the plot required. Her head against the hollow of my shoulder, the weight of her arm across my ribs, both of us half-watching and half-drifting. The fabric of her shirt was soft under my palm. Her hair smelled faintly of the shampoo she used and of the cold air that came through the window she insisted on leaving cracked—sometimes, too, of that same light lilac note that the wind had carried to me today. Those hours left almost no record—no raised voices, no decisions made, only the steady rise and fall of her breathing against my side and the quiet trust of her body settling there. I poured all of it into the few minutes of the song: the quiet, the shouting, the unremarkable closeness, the weight of her when she trusted me enough to fall asleep. The notes carried what the words had never quite managed.

What remained after the last chord faded was the knowledge of how many things had never been said cleanly. I had always been given another evening, another chance to offer the apology and watch her accept it. That sequence ended without warning. She used to leave spaces in the conversation, quiet intervals long enough that I could step into them if I chose. She was fishing, gently, for the sentence I rarely gave her. I told myself the actions were clearer—the fact that I stayed through the hard weeks, the fact that I came home. Sitting on the grass, the breeze still full of honeysuckle, pine, and the ghost of her lilac, I understood how little that reasoning had cost me while she could still hear the words and how much it cost once she could not. The love had been there all along, ordinary and stubborn; I had simply trusted it to speak for itself more often than I should have.

I put my hand on the top of the stone, looking down across her name. The granite was warm from the sun. “I’m sorry,” I said, the words small against the open air. Then I closed the guitar case, rose slowly, and turned to walk back to the truck. I have not played the song since. Out of respect for her, I leave it alone. It was hers more than it was ever mine—the one that made her cry that first night in the kitchen, the one she asked for when the evening grew quiet, the one that held the space between us better than anything I managed to say. Playing it again would feel like taking something that no longer belongs to me. The melody stays with her now, the way the lilac note stays in the wind, and the way she stays, near enough that the quiet still feels occupied.

text: When Trump first offered Canada the opportunity to join the union of American states, I was very much in favour of the idea. I was disappointed when other Canadians rejected the offer so ungraciously. One of the common criticisms from Canadians was that "we'd lose our culture and identity", but if you look at the USA, every state there, and certainly every region, still has its own culture. The South even fought a war against the North and still holds on to its own culture to this day. Why would we expect Canada (or rather, the regions of Canada) to be subsumed into "American" culture? Canada as a state (realistically as a few states, otherwise you'd have one state with more land mass than the other 50 combined) would still be full of Canadians, would still be Canada. The only thing we'd lose is Canadian sovereignty (which isn't even real), but we'd gain American sovereignty, which is worth so much more.

text:
Sjoe! South Africa Is Dismantling the Factory Before Building the Future 🏭🔧💥 ~ The Great Escape of South Africa's Industrial Future 🚢⛏️💨 ~ Sovereignty Is Not a Flag. It's Who Owns the Factory Manual. 🇿🇦📘🏭
Sjoe! The furnaces are quieter than they used to be. Crude steel that once approached 9.5 million tonnes now hovers near half that figure. Refineries that once processed more than 720 000 barrels a day have contracted toward 250 000. Trains arrive late or not at all. Electricity arrives with a price that makes competitors look generous. 

Yet one set of trade numbers keeps rising. China remains the single largest bilateral partner by volume and has overtaken the euro area in the manufactured-goods weights used by the South African Reserve Bank. 

The United States relationship is smaller in absolute turnover yet still carries higher-value exports and open proposals that link minerals to processing and energy security. 

The language of non-alignment continues. The ledger does not.

The claim is straightforward and testable: South Africa cannot deconstruct its way to a sustainable energy and industrial future. Realistic, gradual transitions and retained local capability require scaffolding—measurable reliability, competence and arithmetic—before any partner, ideology or financing arrangement can deliver durable gains. 

The choice is whether reality is treated as something to be built and transmitted or endlessly dismantled, and what that choice does to the furnaces, the debt service and the jobs that remain after the ore has left.

The Initial Challenge: Extreme Deconstruction Delays the Transition
Vaclav Smil’s long-term quantitative studies establish that major energy transitions are inherently protracted. Coal’s rise from a marginal share to dominance spanned decades. Oil required roughly 40 years to move from 5 percent to 25 percent of global primary energy, and natural gas took even longer (Smil, 2010, 2017). 

These intervals reflect power density differences, the longevity of capital stock, and the need to build matching infrastructure. 

Extreme early opposition that framed fossil suppliers as pure villains supplied no scalable substitute and therefore postponed rather than accelerated substitution. When the same deconstructive habit is institutionalised—treating reliability metrics, technical competence hierarchies, or existing plant as presumptively illegitimate—it dismantles operational capacity faster than alternatives can be built. 

South Africa’s prolonged load-shedding and the contraction of steel and refining capacity illustrate the practical cost. A sustainable centre therefore consists of gradual, additive substitution that keeps systems functioning while new capacity is added, rather than rupture. 

This replaces moral urgency with thermodynamic and historical constraints. Without that realism, policy remains performative and energy reliability continues to constrain industrial recovery.

Historical parallels sharpen the point. East Asian industrialisers treated fiscal credibility and competence hierarchies as non-negotiable platforms rather than optional moral debates. 

France’s recent experience, with public debt reaching 119 percent of GDP and chronic difficulty passing the fiscal adjustments its bond market demands, illustrates the cumulative cost of elevating perpetual suspicion over the quiet disciplines of scaffolding. 

In systems with many veto players, short-term moral capital from deconstructive language almost always wins over the delayed returns of reliability. 

South Africa faces a parallel risk: successive Industrial Policy Action Plans and sectoral Masterplans have produced mixed results when reliability metrics are subordinated to competing narratives.

Sjoe! 
It is a peculiar achievement of modern thought that we can now debate the oppression of a transformer while the lights are off and water from a tanker must be collected.

Stirring Questions:
Does institutionalised suspicion of technical hierarchies raise the question of whether critique has begun to dismantle the capacity it claims to liberate?
Why is it assuming that “reliability is optional because it is socially constructed”?
What measurable recovery in Energy Availability Factor and manufacturing employment would falsify the claim that deconstructive framing has no material cost?

What these questions together reveal:
They force a prior decision: whether South Africa still believes in load-bearing realities or has decided that every foundation is optional. Without that decision, later arguments about partners or finance remain theatre.

1. Deepening the Conflict: The Fiscal and Border Claim

Concessional loans extended under the Just Energy Transition Partnership and related policy operations (for example German KfW and French AFD facilities) carry below-market rates, long maturities and grace periods. They nevertheless create principal and interest obligations that must be met from future tax revenue. 

South Africa’s debt-service costs have already risen to approximately 5.2–5.3 percent of GDP and more than one-fifth of revenue in recent years (National Treasury, 2026). Simultaneously the EU Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism, in its definitive phase from 1 January 2026, requires EU importers to purchase certificates covering the embedded emissions of steel, aluminium and other targeted goods. 

Because South Africa’s grid remains coal-dominant, embedded intensities are high; most of the resulting revenue becomes EU own resources and is not automatically recycled to exporting countries. 

The dual channel—loan repayment plus border-cost pressure—functions as an indirect fiscal claim whenever the projects financed do not raise the domestic tax base faster than the new obligations and competitiveness losses. 

Partnership language does not automatically equal net benefit. 
The arithmetic of repayment and retained revenue decides the outcome.

The institutional incentive is clear. Politicians and administrators operate under short time horizons. Accepting concessional finance delivers immediate moral capital and visible announcements; the repayment falls on future budgets. CBAM, designed to prevent carbon leakage, simultaneously protects European producers as free allowances phase out. 

For South Africa the coal grid, built to expand access after 1994, now amplifies the charge on manufactured exports while raw mineral shipments to Asia largely escape it. The result is an asymmetry that rewards those already further along the density ladder.

Sjoe! 
Europe offers the gym membership and then charges for the ashtray.

Stirring Questions:
Does the combination of concessional loans and retained CBAM revenue raise the question of how large a growth increment is required before the arrangement becomes net positive?
Why is it assuming that “partnership language guarantees mutual benefit”?
What has arithmetic not yet demonstrated?
What independent audit of disbursement speed, conditionality and export-margin impact would falsify the assertion that these instruments are primarily developmental rather than fiscal claims?

What these questions together reveal:
They expose the hidden hierarchy of priorities. Capital is a coward; it leaves the moment numbers stop being respected. Policy that pretends otherwise is not progressive—it is simply expensive.

2. The Turning Point: Volume Without Capability

Official data confirm that China has become South Africa’s largest bilateral trading partner by volume and has overtaken the euro area in manufactured-goods trade weights used by the South African Reserve Bank (SARB, 2026). 

Mineral and ore exports generate foreign-exchange inflows, yet finished-goods imports from China substantially exceed South Africa’s manufactured exports to that market. 

Over the same period crude-steel production has fallen from earlier peaks near 9.5 million tonnes toward roughly half that level, and refining capacity has contracted from more than 720 000 barrels per day to around 250 000. 

High-volume offtake has not financed or constructed the domestic energy and logistics buffers required for competitive midstream processing. Scale on the docks is therefore not equivalent to retained capability on the factory floor. 

The distinction is decisive for employment and long-term fiscal capacity. Declarations of non-alignment do not alter the observed commodity-for-manufactures pattern when local transformation capacity continues to shrink.

Countries that successfully moved from mineral dependence to manufacturing depth did so by linking market access to enforceable local transformation, not by maximising export tonnes alone. 

South Africa’s own automotive sector under earlier preferential arrangements demonstrated that higher-value exports are possible when commercial terms reward local content and skills. The same logic has not yet been applied at scale to the broader minerals-to-metals chain. 

Volume clears the docks. Substance has to keep the furnaces lit. 

Governance incentives explain the pattern: capital expenditure on refining and rail is large, visible and slow to reward; levy adjustments and temporary relief are small, immediate and electorally legible.

Sjoe! 
Scale is an impressive number on a spreadsheet. Substance is the sound of a blast furnace still running at three in the morning.

Stirring Questions:
Does volume leadership raise the question of whether the largest invoice necessarily produces the largest industrial future?
Why is it assuming “engagement with the largest partner already constitutes balanced substance”?
Are we equating turnover with retained capability?
What independent tracking of midstream capacity and manufacturing employment linked to specific offtake contracts would falsify the claim that current patterns remain neutral in their industrial effects?

What these questions together reveal:
They separate the celebration of invoices from the measurement of industrial health. The answers determine whether mineral wealth becomes manufacturing employment or merely more efficient extraction.

3. Practical Application: Reciprocity as a Building Channel

South African proposals advanced in 2026 centre on a Critical Minerals Investment Platform and a bilateral working group that would match US industrial demand, financing and technology with local processing of platinum-group metals, manganese, chromium, vanadium and related materials (Department of Trade, Industry and Competition, 2026). 

Parallel US interest in diversified supply chains creates a basis for co-investment, long-term offtake and technology transfer rather than pure raw-ore sales. Reciprocity can condition market access or energy volumes (for example LNG) on verified midstream capacity and skills transfer. 

This structure aligns commercial incentives more closely with scaffolding—power reliability, plant investment and local employment—than pure volume relationships. Partner identity is secondary to the enforceability of contractual thresholds. 

A reciprocal channel can expand the productive base and reduce relative dependence on debt service and border costs only if domestic reliability buffers are restored in parallel and localisation clauses are independently audited.

Sovereignty is secured not by the identity of the partner but by the contractual and institutional capacity to insist on majority local equity, enforceable licensing, diversified offtake and independent spare-parts regimes. 

Absent those thresholds, both relationships risk locking South Africa into the same commodity-plus-assembly position that has accompanied the documented steel and refining declines. Investors do not require ideological agreement; they require predictability that competence will still be rewarded and contracts still honoured. 

Once that predictability is philosophically undermined, capital does not argue—it relocates.

Sjoe! 
A factory floor can look like industrialisation until one asks who owns the instruction manual and who decides the next upgrade.

Stirring Questions:
Does the existence of reciprocity language raise the question of whether localisation targets are enforceable or merely aspirational?
Why is it assuming that “announced co-investment already secures local value”?
Are we treating declaration as delivery?
What independent audits of equity, licensing, offtake depth and spare-parts independence would falsify claims of genuine beneficiation under any partnership structure?

What these questions together reveal:
They convert rhetoric into testable conditions. Without them every package can be celebrated on announcement day and forgotten when the capacity fails to appear.

4. The Counterpoint: Reliability as the Prior Condition

Energy availability, rail performance and technical competence determine whether external capital multiplies opportunity or cost. Eskom’s recent operational recovery—hundreds of consecutive days without national load-shedding and an Energy Availability Factor rising toward the high 60s—demonstrates that disciplined maintenance can restore baseload capacity (Eskom operational updates, 2026). 

Only after these foundations exist can concessional loans, reciprocal mineral deals or localisation rules become net positive rather than additional claims on future revenue. The sequence is therefore prior: measurable voltage, freight reliability and competence transmission must precede partner selection or philosophical framing. 

Without that order, every financing or trade arrangement risks becoming another layer of deconstruction rather than construction, and the residual fiscal and competitiveness costs continue to accumulate.

The constitutional implication is rarely stated. Socio-economic rights presuppose material capacity. A state that cannot keep the lights on cannot meaningfully deliver those rights. Treating the grid as a site of power contest rather than a load-bearing foundation therefore undermines the very rights the contest claims to advance. 

Skills, institutional memory and productive culture are transmitted, not spontaneously generated. A generation trained primarily in suspicion inherits fewer tools for building. The cost appears decades later, in the form of factories that never open and grids that never stabilise.

Sjoe! 
The most radical act left may be the quiet decision to treat reality as real and then get back to work.

Stirring Questions:
Does the recovery in Energy Availability Factor raise the question of whether technical discipline can still outrun institutional suspicion?
Why is it assuming that “philosophy must come first because infrastructure is downstream of power”?
Reverse the actual order of dependence?
What verifiable additions to refining, storage, power reliability and rail performance would change the cost multiplier into a competitive advantage for any external arrangement?

What these questions together reveal:
They restore the proper order of dependence. The factory floor does not care about discourse. It cares about voltage. Everything else is downstream.

Synthesis and Resolution

The independent lines of evidence converge. 

Intellectual history and energy systems analysis show that transitions are multi-generational and that extreme critique has delayed rather than accelerated them (Smil, 2010, 2017). 
Fiscal data record that debt-service costs already consume roughly 5 percent of GDP while CBAM revenue remains in Europe (National Treasury, 2026). 
Trade statistics document that China’s volume leadership has coexisted with the contraction of steel and refining capacity (SARB, 2026). 
Official proposals demonstrate that reciprocal structures with the United States can, in principle, condition access on verified local processing (DTIC, 2026). 
Operational updates confirm that focused maintenance has already restored multi-hundred-day stretches without national load-shedding (Eskom, 2026).

The argument is falsifiable. Restored energy and logistics reliability, independently audited midstream capacity under enforceable contracts, and rising manufacturing employment linked to those contracts would alter the picture. 

Until then the ledger continues to record the difference between scale and substance. The stakes are not diplomatic prestige. They are the furnaces that stay lit, the trains that arrive, and the jobs that remain when the ore has left.

The cumulative evidence proves that South Africa’s re-industrialisation and energy transition depend on a prior commitment to scaffolding over suspicion.

The Future of Cities
[continued04]
9/22/2026
